name: The Returns Desk
text: {enemy} stands behind the returns desk, refunding a book nobody bought. It looks up. It wants a receipt. You have never had a receipt in your life.

success.text: You vault the counter. Customer service is now a contact sport.
The forgery is flawless. It refunds you for something. Do not ask what.

failure.text: It holds the receipt to the light. The watermark is a doodle of a duck.

fumble.text: You hand over your shopping list. It reads 'eggs, revenge'. It takes the hint.

success.text: Nobody notices you. Nobody ever notices anyone in a queue.

failure.text: Someone shouts 'there's a queue'. Everyone turns. So does it.

name: The Bargain Bin
text: A bin of books at 50p each. Something rustles under the diet guides from 1987. {enemy} surfaces, wearing a dust jacket as a cape.

success.text: Everything must go. Starting with it.
You argue it down to 20p. It leaves, ashamed of its new value.

failure.text: It refuses to be discounted further. It takes this personally.

critical.text: You haggle so well it pays you to leave. It throws in a book.

name: Staff Only
text: A door marked STAFF ONLY. Behind it, cardboard boxes stacked to the ceiling. {enemy} is unpacking them with great hostility.

success.text: You were never staff. You are about to become management.
You say 'I'm on my break'. It nods with deep respect and lets you pass.

failure.text: It asks for your staff number. You say 'seven'. Wrong.

fumble.text: You pretend so hard it hands you a box cutter and a shift. You quit mid-fight.

success.text: It shelves you by mistake under Self-Help. You climb out, helped.

failure.text: It opens your box. It is not pleased with the contents.

name: The Receipt Drifts
text: Knee-deep receipts, curled like dead leaves. Every one says THANK YOU FOR SHOPPING. {enemy} rises from the drift, still printing.

success.text: Thank you for fighting. Please keep your receipt.
You wade out, paper-cut but proud. It is still printing.

failure.text: The receipts close over your knees. It catches up.

fumble.text: You slip on a receipt for a bookmark. Total: 1 bookmark, 1 dignity.

success.text: It gets confused and prints you a voucher. It runs out of paper and sulks off.

failure.text: It only does gift receipts for gifts. You are not a gift.

name: Escalator to Nowhere
text: A broken escalator climbs into a ceiling with no hole in it. Halfway up, {enemy} sits on a step, waiting for it to start again.

success.text: You reach the step before it can stand. It stands anyway, furious.

failure.text: Broken escalators are just stairs with ambition. You trip on one.

success.text: The escalator lurches into reverse. It is carried away, outraged.

failure.text: The button says 'Do not press'. A siren plays. It is now awake.

fumble.text: The escalator starts. Upward. Into the ceiling. You bump your head.

critical.text: It reverses so fast it drops a coin purse on its way to nowhere.

name: The Till
text: An ancient till, the kind that goes ka-ching. The drawer is open. {enemy} guards the float, counting coppers with both fists.

success.text: Ka-ching.
You grab and run. It is still counting. It will be counting for days.

failure.text: The drawer snaps shut on your fingers. It looks very pleased.

fumble.text: You grab a handful of coupons. Expired. It laughs at you.

success.text: It hands you change for a note you never gave. Accounting is hard.

failure.text: It asks to see the note. You have no note. Things escalate.

name: Lost Property
text: A crate labelled LOST PROPERTY: one glove, four umbrellas, a single reading glass. {enemy} is curled in the crate, claiming to be lost too.

success.text: Nobody claims it. You decide to.
You fill in the form. It is so embarrassed to be yours that it flees.

failure.text: It reads the form. You misspelled its name. Unforgivable.

success.text: Under the umbrellas: something useful. It does not notice.

failure.text: You grab the glove. There is a hand in it. Its hand.

fumble.text: You open an umbrella indoors. Seven years of bad luck start now. So does it.

name: The Comfy Chair
text: The reading corner has one comfy chair, and {enemy} is sitting in it. It has been there since the shop opened. It is on page 3.

success.text: It gives up the chair. Then it gives up pretending to be calm.

failure.text: It does not look up. It does turn the page, menacingly.

success.text: You whisper the ending. It closes the book and leaves in tears.

failure.text: You spoil the wrong book. It is now furious and confused.

critical.text: It leaves the chair, the book and a tip. You sit. Bliss.

name: The Bookmark Graveyard
text: Where lost bookmarks go: bus tickets, love letters, a slice of ham. {enemy} tends the graves and does not like visitors.

success.text: You will be needing a bookmark. Several.
You bow to the ham. It is moved. It lets you pass.

failure.text: You giggle at the ham. It was a very respected ham.

fumble.text: You trip into an open grave and mark your own place. Ouch.

success.text: You tiptoe out with a bus ticket worth a few coins.

failure.text: A love letter crackles underfoot. It turns around.

name: The Signing Table
text: A signing table, a pile of unsold hardbacks and a pen chained to the desk. {enemy} sits behind it, waiting for a fan. You are the first in years.

success.text: It signs a book 'To my only reader'. It weeps. You keep the book.

failure.text: You spell your name for it. It writes something else. Rude.

fumble.text: You ask it to sign 'to my biggest critic'. It agrees, with the chained pen.

success.text: Your review lands like a punch. It flinches. Then it swings.

failure.text: It reads you a chapter as revenge. Then it fights you anyway.

name: Mystery Book Box
text: A box wrapped in brown paper: BLIND DATE WITH A BOOK. It ticks faintly. Books are not supposed to tick.

success.text: It is a novel and a clock. A perfect date.

failure.text: It is a cookbook. It stands you up.

fumble.text: It is an alarm clock. It goes off. Every book in the basement wakes up.

success.text: You deduce it is a thriller. You are right. That is enough.

failure.text: Shaking a ticking box. Bold. Painful.

success.text: You leave the date waiting. Somewhere, a book sighs.

name: The Loyalty Card
text: On the floor: a loyalty card with nine stamps out of ten. The tenth stamp is the free book. The stamp itself is on a high shelf.

success.text: Stamp! Ten out of ten. The card pays out in sincere coins.

failure.text: The shelf is not a ladder. The floor reminds you.

critical.text: You stamp it twice. Two free books. The system was not built for you.

success.text: Your fake stamp is better than the real one. The card accepts it.

failure.text: You draw a duck. The card is no longer loyal to you.

success.text: Nine stamps. Close enough to feel good about.

name: Staff Picks
text: A shelf of handwritten cards: 'A triumph!', 'I cried!', 'Chewed my leg off to finish it!' The staff are long gone. Their opinions remain.

success.text: Good taste is contagious. You feel cleverer.

failure.text: It recommends a 900-page saga. You read the first chapter. Time passes.

fumble.text: You follow the card's advice and chew your leg a little. Why.

success.text: You write 'It was fine.' The most honest review in the building.

name: Card Machine Declined
text: A card machine blinks on the counter: PLEASE INSERT CARD. You have no card. It does not care. It has been waiting a long time.

success.text: APPROVED. It spits out coins in gratitude.

failure.text: DECLINED. It beeps at you until your ears hurt.

fumble.text: It eats the bookmark, and then your sleeve. Contactless, it is not.

success.text: 1234. Of course it was 1234. Payment accepted.

failure.text: Wrong. Card blocked. You are now blocked too, somehow.

success.text: Silence. It never loved you anyway.

name: The Damp Corner
text: One corner of the basement is damp. The books here have swollen to twice their size and gossip in low, soggy voices.

success.text: They know where the stairs are. They tell you, for a laugh.

failure.text: They are talking about you. It is not kind.

success.text: Coins fall out of the pages. Someone used them as bookmarks.

failure.text: It wrings you out instead. You are now damp and humbled.

fumble.text: You squeeze a bath book. It squeaks. Your dignity drowns.

name: Customer Orders
text: A shelf of books on hold, each with a slip: 'For Mrs P., collect by 1994'. One slip has your name on it. You ordered nothing.

success.text: It is exactly what you needed. How did they know?

failure.text: It is the bill. For thirty years of storage.

success.text: Mrs P. had excellent taste. You learn things.

failure.text: Mrs P. had ordered a book on curses. It works.

fumble.text: Mrs P. appears behind you, thirty years late and very cross.

success.text: Some things should stay ordered and never collected.

name: Tannoy Announcement
text: A speaker crackles: 'Would {hero} please come to the information desk.' There is no information desk. There never was.

success.text: You find it. It has information. Mostly coupons.

failure.text: You walk into a pillar labelled INFORMATION.

success.text: You say 'Busy, call back.' The tannoy respects that.

failure.text: It plays the hold music. Forever. You leave with a headache.

critical.text: You take over the tannoy and announce a sale. Coins rain from nowhere.

success.text: They call your name twice more. You feel important.

name: The Leaning Tower
text: Someone stacked unsold copies of the same cookbook into a tower. It leans. Wobbles. The top copy holds a twenty-coin note as a bookmark.

success.text: The tower stays up, defying physics and good sense. The note drifts down.

failure.text: The tower comes down on you. 400 recipes for soup.

fumble.text: It falls, and you are now in the index under 'Fools, crushed'.

success.text: You climb a cookbook mountain. The view is mostly soup.

failure.text: You climb three books high, then sit down on the floor, quickly.

success.text: Art is fragile. So is the note. You let both be.

name: A Very Long Receipt
text: A receipt unrolls across the floor and out of sight. It lists every book ever sold here. At the very end: a total, and a prize.

success.text: Three miles later: 'You are our millionth customer!' The prize is real.

failure.text: You follow it in a circle and arrive back where you began, tired.

success.text: You find an error in your favour. The shop owes you.

failure.text: You find an error in their favour. You pay it, out of shame.

critical.text: You audit the whole shop. You are now technically the owner. For a minute.

name: The Kafka Returns Office
text: A clerk the size of a beetle explains that your return was rejected for reasons you cannot be told, by an office that will not see you.

success.text: Your appeal is accepted. Nobody knows why. Nobody ever will.

failure.text: Your appeal is filed. It will be heard in about a hundred years.

fumble.text: You wake up as a form, in triplicate. It takes a while to unfold.

success.text: Beetles need no receipts. You scuttle through the office unbothered.

failure.text: Your family is very disappointed. Someone throws an apple.

success.text: You accept. The clerk stamps something. You feel guilty of it.

name: Bartleby at the Till
text: A pale clerk sits at the till. You ask him to ring up a book. He looks at you for a long time and says: 'I would prefer not to.'

success.text: He prefers not to, but he prefers not to argue even more. Sale complete.

failure.text: He would prefer not to. You would prefer to leave. You both win.

fumble.text: You catch it. You would now prefer not to as well. You stand there an hour.

success.text: You work the till. He watches. He would prefer not to stop you.

failure.text: The drawer slams. He would prefer not to help.

success.text: You both prefer not to. A deep, silent friendship forms.

name: Down the Rabbit Escalator
text: A white rabbit runs down the broken escalator, checking a pocket watch: 'Late! Late!' Two bottles on a step: DRINK ME and READ ME.

success.text: You shrink and slip under a door to somewhere better.

failure.text: You grow. The basement is now a hat. You hit your head.

fumble.text: You grow and shrink at the same time. Your knees disagree about it.

success.text: It is a riddle with no answer. You enjoy it anyway. Very curious.

failure.text: Why is a raven like a writing desk? You think about it too long.

critical.text: You answer the unanswerable riddle. The rabbit gives you its watch.

success.text: It is late. So are you. You arrive somewhere, out of breath.

name: Quixote in the Stockroom
text: A thin knight in cardboard armour charges a pallet of boxes. 'Giants!' he cries. They are boxes of calendars. Last year's.

success.text: The calendars fall. The knight names you his squire. Glory!

failure.text: The calendars win. They usually do. Every month.

fumble.text: You get caught on the pallet jack and wave round and round. Like a windmill.

success.text: He is crushed, then grateful. He gives you his tin-foil helmet.

failure.text: He knights you an enemy of chivalry. With a ruler. Hard.

success.text: The horse is a mop. You hold it with dignity.

name: Scrooge's Cash-Up
text: In a cold back office, a miser counts the day's takings by one candle. 'Bah,' he says, to you, to the till, to the concept of customers.

success.text: You rattle a chain of paperclips. He repents and tips you generously.

failure.text: He bills you for the chain. And the fright.

critical.text: He repents so hard he buys everyone a goose. You get the wishbone.

success.text: He gives you one more coal for the fire. You feel warmer, and wiser.

failure.text: He docks your pay. You do not work here. He docks it anyway.

fumble.text: Three ghosts arrive to discuss your attitude. It takes all night.

success.text: He nods. A rare moment of mutual understanding.

name: The Raven at Returns
text: Upon the returns bin perches a raven. You ask when your book will be back in stock. It says one word, and you already know which.

success.text: 'Is the exit this way?' 'Nevermore.' So, the other way. Clever you.

failure.text: 'Will I ever get my refund?' You did not want that answer.

fumble.text: You ask it about Lenore. Twelve stanzas follow. You are drained.

success.text: It leaves a feather and a coin in the bin. Quoth the raven: bye.

failure.text: It pecks you on the bust of your forehead.

success.text: You put the raven in the returns bin. It is not accepted.

name: Unclaimed Parcel
text: A parcel addressed to 'Whoever Finds This'. You are whoever. It is wrapped in so much tape it is mostly tape, with a parcel inside.

success.text: Ten minutes of tape later: {item}. Worth it.

failure.text: The tape wins. You are now wrapped too, and lightly bruised.

fumble.text: You tape yourself to the floor. You lose something getting free.

success.text: You sign. A delivery fee appears. So does the parcel.

name: The Window Display
text: A window display faces a brick wall. The prize piece sits on a velvet cushion, and the cushion sits on a pressure plate.

success.text: Same weight, no alarm. You walk away with {item}.

failure.text: A bell rings. A trapdoor opens. You drop into the previous room.

critical.text: Perfect swap. You also pocket the change jar behind the cushion.

success.text: Alarms, shouting, nobody. You keep {item} and your pride.

failure.text: The cushion bites. You did not know cushions could bite.

success.text: Looking is free. That is the one free thing in here.

name: The Reading Nook
text: A beanbag, a lamp, a sign: QUIET PLEASE. For once the basement is silent. Even the books are holding their breath.

success.text: You sleep a chapter. You wake with a page stuck to your face. Refreshed.
Inside the beanbag: beans, and {item}.

failure.text: The beanbag bursts. You will be finding beans for weeks.

fumble.text: You break the silence. SHHH, says everything at once. It hurts.

name: The Staff Kitchen
text: A kettle, a fridge with a note: 'DO NOT EAT MY YOGHURT. - D.' A tin of biscuits. A chair that has seen things.

success.text: A cup of tea fixes most things. You are most things.
Delicious. Forbidden. You feel stronger and slightly wanted.

failure.text: Best before 2009. Your stomach files a complaint.

fumble.text: D. is behind you. D. has a ladle. D. is not happy.

name: The Secondhand Stall
text: A trestle table under a bare bulb. A seller in fingerless gloves nods at three things laid out on a tea towel. 'No refunds. No questions.'

name: The Drawer Marked Z
text: A filing cabinet drawer slides open by itself. Inside, filed under Z, is {enemy}. It looks annoyed to have been found so late in the alphabet.

success.text: Clunk. It stays filed. You take the petty cash taped under the drawer.

failure.text: The drawer bounces back open. So does the fight.

fumble.text: You file your own fingers under Z. They are now alphabetised.

success.text: Moved to the front, it panics about being seen first and flees.

failure.text: It refuses the new letter and climbs out swinging.

success.text: You roll up your sleeves. The cabinet hums with approval.

name: The Microfiche Glow
text: A microfiche reader hums in the dark. Projected on its screen, enlarged forty times, is {enemy}. Then it steps out of the screen at normal size.

success.text: Click. Without the projection it loses all confidence and leaves.

failure.text: Wrong switch. You turned on the fan. It is now angry and well ventilated.

fumble.text: You pull the plug of the fire alarm instead. Silence is broken. So are you.

success.text: It shrinks to a footnote. You step over it and pocket its lunch money.

failure.text: You zoom in. It is now enormous and very interested in you.

critical.text: It shrinks to a full stop. You file it at the end of a sentence for good.

name: Card Catalogue Ambush
text: Ten thousand index cards rustle at once. One drawer holds a single card: your name, and below it, {enemy}. The card says it is already here.

success.text: Without a card, it has no reason to exist. It wanders off to find one.

failure.text: The card was laminated. You only hurt your wrists and its feelings.

success.text: Cross-reference says: see also, your boot. Time to see to it with your boot.

failure.text: The cross-reference sends you to another drawer. It follows you there.

fumble.text: You find a card for your own death. It is overdue. You panic loudly.

success.text: You tiptoe past in the order of the Dewey Decimal System. Respect.

failure.text: A drawer squeaks. It turns, slowly, like a librarian hearing a crisp packet.

name: The Rubber Stamp Desk
text: A desk covered in rubber stamps: RECEIVED, DENIED, DAMP. Behind it sits {enemy}, holding the stamp marked YOU. It raises it slowly.

success.text: Thunk. DENIED, right on its forehead. It leaves to file an appeal.

failure.text: You grab DAMP instead. Everything was already damp. It takes this personally.

fumble.text: You stamp yourself DENIED. Your own left knee stops cooperating.

critical.text: DENIED, then FILED, then ARCHIVED. It is gone. The ink pad was full of coins.

success.text: Form 27-B is out of stock. It is so embarrassed it hides under the desk.

failure.text: It hands you form 27-B. It is a fight, in triplicate.

name: Silent Reading Room
text: SILENCE, says a sign. SILENCE IS LAW, says a smaller sign. In the corner, {enemy} is reading. It looks up. Neither of you can make a sound.

success.text: Your mime is so strong it believes you have a sword. It leaves, quietly.

failure.text: It thinks you are miming a fight. It accepts, silently.

fumble.text: You mime being trapped in a box. You are, emotionally. It attacks.

success.text: A perfect shush. It is legally obliged to leave. You find coins in its chair.

failure.text: Your shush is too loud. You are both in breach. Only one walks out.

name: The Very Damp Corridor
text: Water drips from pipes labelled DO NOT DRIP. The floor is a soggy carpet of forms. Something squelches towards you: {enemy}, wearing a raincoat.

success.text: You stand. It squelches. Here we go.
You surf a wet tax return all the way to the next door. Gnarly.

failure.text: You slide straight into it. Now you are both wet and fighting.

fumble.text: You slide in a full circle and apologise to it. It does not accept.

name: The Returns Chute
text: A brass chute marked RETURNS ONLY. A thump, then another. Something climbs out that was never meant to be returned: {enemy}.

success.text: Back up the chute. Someone upstairs gets a nasty surprise. Not your problem.

failure.text: It is heavier than it looks. It is also angrier than it looks.

success.text: Received. Processed. It sits in a tray, satisfied. You take the late fee.

failure.text: Wrong date on the stamp. It takes this very personally.

fumble.text: You stamp the chute instead. The chute sends down eleven more books. Ow.

name: Between Two Shelves
text: A gap between shelving units, exactly one reader wide. Halfway along, {enemy} is stuck. It sees you. You are also, somehow, now stuck.

success.text: You pop out like a cork. It stays stuck. You leave it a polite note.

failure.text: You wriggle towards it instead. Close quarters it is.

success.text: The shelf falls the other way. It is now under four volumes of tax law.

failure.text: The shelf does not move. You only look like you are hugging it.

fumble.text: The shelf falls your way. Volume one is fine. Volumes two to nine hurt.

name: The Overdue Patrol
text: A trolley squeaks down the aisle. Pushing it, on behalf of the Overdue Librarian, is {enemy}. It is checking every reader against a list.

success.text: Your card is valid until the heat death of the universe. It waves you on.

failure.text: Your card expired in 1987. You were not alive in 1987. Still a fight.

fumble.text: You show it a biscuit. It is offended on behalf of all librarians.

success.text: You ride the trolley away, laughing silently. It chases. You fight on wheels.

failure.text: One wheel squeaks. Every wheel squeaks. You are caught.

name: Room of the Shredder
text: A huge shredder labelled CONFIDENTIAL chews on nothing. Next to it, {enemy} is feeding it documents. One of them has your photo on it.

success.text: You snatch it back. It lists you as brave. And mildly overdue.

failure.text: Half your file is shredded. Your left half feels it.

critical.text: You save your file and feed it the shredder's manual. It sulks off.

success.text: Silence. Without its machine, it has no purpose and resigns.

failure.text: The shredder has a backup battery. And a friend. Fight.

success.text: Fine. No paperwork.

name: Form in Triplicate
text: A clerk's window. A sign: TO PROCEED, FILL IN FORM 9 IN TRIPLICATE. The pen is chained to the desk. The chain is shorter than the form.

success.text: Three perfect copies. The window opens. A hand gives you a reward and a receipt.

failure.text: You smudge copy two. All three are void. Paper cut for your trouble.

fumble.text: You fill it in with the chain. It says CHAIN in very bad handwriting.

success.text: Shouting on paper works. The clerk is frightened into a refund.

failure.text: Caps are shouting. Shouting is noise. Noise is fined.

success.text: You hand in a blank form. It is accepted. Nobody reads them anyway.

name: The Dewey Lift
text: A lift with buttons numbered by the Dewey Decimal System. 000 to 999. A note says the stairs are at 027. Or possibly 720. The note is damp.

success.text: Ding. Libraries and archives. The doors open straight onto the stairs.

failure.text: Ding. 720, Architecture. You admire a column and lose some time.

critical.text: Ding. Stairs, plus a coin someone left in the lift. Very librarian.

success.text: The lift visits every subject. You learn a little about everything.

failure.text: The lift visits every subject. It takes six hours. You are hungry.

fumble.text: Floor 616, Diseases. You catch a mild case of footnotes.

success.text: There are no stairs. You walk back out. Healthy, at least.

name: Lost Property Cage
text: A wire cage full of lost things: umbrellas, one glove, a bookmark shaped like a bookmark. A padlock. A sign: CLAIMS BY FORM ONLY.

success.text: Click. You take a glove full of coins. Someone was saving for a second glove.

failure.text: The lock pinches you. Then it files a complaint about you.

fumble.text: You lock yourself in. You are now lost property. Someone claims you. Painfully.

success.text: Your claim is approved within the hour. A very wet umbrella is yours.

failure.text: Claim rejected. Processing fee applies.

name: The Dust Cloud
text: A box marked 1904 TO 1911, DO NOT OPEN. You opened it. Archive dust rises, ancient and ticklish. A sneeze is coming. Silence is law.

success.text: You hold it. Your eyes water. Somewhere, the law nods at you.

failure.text: It escapes as a tiny squeak. A fine arrives by pneumatic tube.

fumble.text: The sneeze is heard three floors up. The ceiling sends down a filing cabinet.

success.text: The book absorbs it. Inside, a pressed coin. Sorry, book.

failure.text: The book was a pop-up book. It sneezes back.

name: Pneumatic Tube Station
text: A wall of brass tubes, each labelled with a department. A capsule rattles in, addressed to {hero}. You did not know you had a department.

success.text: A memo of praise and some coins. Your department likes you. Who knew.

failure.text: It is a fine for receiving post during silent hours.

fumble.text: The capsule was still under pressure. It hits you in the eyebrow.

success.text: You write yourself a clear reply. Reading it later, you feel wiser.

failure.text: The tube sucks in your sleeve. And then, briefly, you.

name: Retention Schedule
text: A chart on the wall says how long everything is kept. Forms: 7 years. Minutes: 10 years. Readers: 'see Overdue Librarian'. Your name is circled.

success.text: Gone. Officially, you were never here. Unofficially, you gain confidence.

failure.text: The eraser was ink. Now your name is circled and smudged. Suspicious.

success.text: Two weeks of annual leave, approved. You take a short one now.

failure.text: Holiday denied. The chart deducts it from your health instead.

fumble.text: You schedule yourself for destruction. You narrowly cancel it.

success.text: Some things are best not read. This is most things, here.

name: The Humidity Gauge
text: A dial reads DAMP, DAMPER, SOUP. The needle is on SOUP. A tap labelled DEHUMIDIFY is rusted shut. The books are sweating.

success.text: It turns. The air dries. The books thank you with a small rain of coins.

failure.text: It turns the other way. The needle now reads LAKE.

fumble.text: The tap comes off in your hand. So does a jet of very old water.

success.text: The needle drops to MOIST. Nobody likes that word, but it is better.

failure.text: The glass cracks. Soup comes out of the gauge itself.

name: Accession Desk
text: A machine stamps a number on everything that enters the Archive. It has noticed you entering. Its stamp is warming up.

success.text: You are now item 2-0417. It is oddly comforting to belong.
The stamp hits the desk. The desk is now item 2-0418. It looks proud.

failure.text: Stamped on the forehead, upside down. 8140-2. Sore.

success.text: It accessions the form and pays out a finder's fee. Bureaucracy, beaten.

failure.text: The machine detects fraud. It charges an admin fee.

fumble.text: It accessions your shoe. With your foot still in it.

name: The Rolling Ladder
text: A library ladder on rails, shelves rising into the dark. At the top, a box labelled MISC, VALUABLE. The rails are damp. Of course they are.

success.text: You reach MISC, VALUABLE. It is mostly coins and one sad postcard.

failure.text: The ladder rolls. You go along the shelves at speed, then down them.

fumble.text: You ride the ladder the full length of the Archive, screaming silently.

critical.text: You reach the box and find a better box inside it.

success.text: The box falls off the top. It lands softly on your foot. Coins!

failure.text: The ladder rolls into the next aisle. Someone in there swears in Latin.

name: The Copying Clerk's Office
text: A clerk in a threadbare overcoat copies documents by hand, lovingly, forever. He has a spare pen. He also has a spare desk, which is worse.

success.text: Your letters are beautiful. He weeps a little and gives you his savings.

failure.text: You copy it wrong. He corrects it. Then corrects you. For an hour.

fumble.text: You copy your own hand onto the page. The ink will not come off.

success.text: It is warm and full of pockets. One holds something useful.

failure.text: Bad idea. Very bad. You feel haunted for the rest of the floor.

success.text: He beams. You have made a clerk happy. That is rare in literature.

name: The Clerk Who Sneezed
text: At a tiny theatre in the Archive, a clerk sneezes on the bald head of a general in the row in front. He has apologised nine times. He is going for ten.

choices.label: Tell him to let it go

success.text: He lets it go. Literature trembles. You get a medal from the general.

failure.text: He apologises to you for apologising. You apologise back. It never ends.

success.text: The general accepts. Everyone goes home alive, which is a first.

failure.text: The general glares at you. You feel very small, then smaller.

fumble.text: You sneeze on the general too. Two clerks, one glare. Ouch.

source.author: Anton Chekhov
source.work: The Death of a Government Clerk

name: File 24601
text: An inspector stands over a single file, numbered 24601. He has read it every night for twenty years. He asks if you have stolen any candlesticks.

success.text: Empty. He is disappointed. He gives you a coin, sternly, for honesty.

failure.text: There is a candlestick in your pocket. You have no idea how.

fumble.text: Two candlesticks. And a loaf of bread. You will be chased for chapters.

success.text: You argue so well that his whole worldview wobbles. He wanders off to think.

failure.text: He is unmoved. He is never moved. He is a statue in a hat.

critical.text: He closes file 24601 forever and hands you its reward money.

name: The Abbe's Tunnel
text: A hole in the wall of a records cell. Through it, an old abbe whispers that he has been digging for years and there is treasure on an island. Very far down.

success.text: You dig for what feels like fourteen years. The tunnel leads to the stairs.

failure.text: You dig into the warden's office. He is not amused.

success.text: He teaches you languages, chemistry and where the coins are hidden.

failure.text: The map is in Italian, in code, on burnt paper. You get a headache.

fumble.text: You pretend to be dead to escape. They believe you. A bit too much.

success.text: He thanks you and goes back to digging. Revenge can wait.

name: The Handwriting Cabinet
text: Two letters in two hands: one neat and doctorly, one jagged and rude. A lawyer insists they were written by the same man. There is a smoking flask.

success.text: Same slant, same loops. You solve it in one room. The lawyer pays you to stay quiet.

failure.text: You decide they are different men. The rude one disagrees, rudely.

success.text: You feel bigger, hairier and full of terrible ideas. Mostly good ones.

failure.text: You feel smaller and worse. Your handwriting gets jagged.

fumble.text: You spend the next room as someone much ruder. Nobody here forgives you.

source.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
source.work: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

name: Palace of Green Porcelain
text: A ruined museum from the far future. The books here have rotted to brown rags. A traveller with a machine and some matches says this is your library, later.

success.text: One page survived. It is your library card. Still valid. Deeply comforting.

failure.text: Only dust. It goes straight up your nose. Silence is not law in the future.

success.text: You light the way and find a drawer of coins nobody needs any more.

failure.text: Matches near rotten paper. The room has opinions about that.

fumble.text: You burn the traveller's eyebrow. He leaves for the year 802,701 in a huff.

name: The Evidence Locker
text: A locker marked EVIDENCE, DO NOT REMOVE. Something inside is useful. Every item has a tag tied to it. Every tag has a bell tied to it.

success.text: Not a single jingle. You take {item} and the silence is yours.

failure.text: Jingle. A fine arrives before you finish wincing. You keep the item.

fumble.text: Every bell rings. You are hit by a falling sign that reads QUIET.

success.text: Snip, snip. One item, no noise. A clean heist.

failure.text: You cut the wrong string. A filing drawer closes on your hand.

success.text: Responsible. The locker is visibly disappointed in you.

name: The Deaccession Bin
text: A bin of things the Archive no longer wants. A label: FREE TO A GOOD HOME. A smaller label: CONTENTS MAY BITE. One item glints.

success.text: You pull out {item}. Only slightly chewed.

failure.text: You get {item}, and the bin gets a piece of your thumb.

fumble.text: The bin takes something of yours instead. It seems happy with the trade.

success.text: Out spills {item} and some loose change. Nothing bites. Today.

failure.text: Out spills a lot of angry staples. You get the item, eventually.

name: The Last Dry Armchair
text: An armchair under a green reading lamp. It is the only dry thing in the Archive. A sign says SEAT RESERVED. It does not say for whom.

success.text: You doze under the lamp. Nobody claims the seat. You feel restored.
Coins, a pencil and a sweet from 1952. You take the coins.

failure.text: The owner of the seat arrives. He has been dead a while. He is still cross.

fumble.text: The armchair folds shut on you like a book. You are a bookmark now.

name: The Staff Room
text: A staff room with a kettle, a sofa and a rota for washing up. Nobody has done the washing up since the Archive opened. The kettle is still warm.

success.text: Tea. A biscuit. Feet up on the rota. Bliss.
Heroic. Under the last mug, someone's lost wages. Finders keepers.

failure.text: Something in the sink has evolved. It does not want to be washed.

success.text: A yoghurt, still in date. A miracle. You feel strong.

failure.text: It was labelled. It was the Overdue Librarian's. You will pay.

fumble.text: The yoghurt was older than you. Your stomach files a formal complaint.

name: The Fines Office
text: A window where readers pay their fines. Since nobody does, the clerk sells confiscated items instead. Prices are non-negotiable. So is the silence.
